summary: Wilhelm von Humboldt worked in linguistics, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at Frankfurt (Oder), European University Viadrina, Göttingen, and Jena under Engel, von Dohm, Klein, Lichtenberg, Heyne, and Chézy. He served as Prussian Minister (~1819) and at Humboldt University of Berlin.

Wilhelm von Pochhammer was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed his studies across the universities of Freiburg (~1910–1911), Marburg (~1911–1912), Munich (~1912–1913), and Bonn (~1913–1914).

Will Sweetman is a religious studies and Indology scholar. He studied at the University of Cambridge (~1988–1991) and Lancaster University (~1992–1996). He held posts at the University of Newcastle (~1999–2005), University of Otago (~2005), and Australia India Institute (~2016).

Will Tuladhar-Douglas works in religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Oxford under Edwin Gerow. He held posts at Wolfson College, Oxford, Aberdeen (attested 2009–2015), Toronto Scarborough (2010), ICIMOD (2013), and Hamburg (2020–2026).

Willard Gurdon Oxtoby studied religion and Iranian and Central Asian studies at Stanford, Princeton, and Harvard. He taught at McGill (1960–1964) and Yale (1966–1971), then served as professor at Trinity College and University of Toronto (1971–1999).

Willard L. Johnson worked in Indology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Oberlin College and the University of Wisconsin-Madison. His career included posts at California State University, San Diego State University, Del Mar College, and Oberlin College.

Willard Van Orman Quine was a philosopher and linguist. Educated at Oberlin and Harvard under Rudolf Carnap and Alfred North Whitehead, he spent his career largely at Harvard University (1933–1978), holding the Edgar Pierce Chair of Philosophy from 1948.

Willem Bollée was an Indologist who studied under Jan Gonda at Utrecht University (~1946–1956) and completed his Habilitation at Hamburg (~1972–1975). He held posts as Assistant Professor at Münster (1971–1978) and Lecturer/Professor at Heidelberg University (~1977–1993).

Willem Caland worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Leiden University (1877–1883) under Carel Gabriel Cobet and Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern. He later served at Stedelijk Gymnasium Breda and held the Chair of Sanskrit at Utrecht University (1906–1930).

Willem Frederik Stutterheim was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Utrecht and Leiden under Nicolaas Johannes Krom. He later served in the Oudheidkundige Dienst, directed Surakarta College (1926–1936), and directed Dinas Purbakala (1937).

Willem Lodewijk van Helten was a linguist who studied under Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern at Leiden University (1865–1871). He taught at Gymnasium Erasmianum (~1873–1882) and served as Professor at the University of Groningen (1882–1911).

Willem van der Molen is a scholar of linguistics, history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Leiden University (~1971–1983) and later held academic posts at Leiden University (~1979–2017) and the University of Indonesia.

William A. Magee is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins, later serving as professor there (attested 1992) and teaching at the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2008).

William Abbott Oldfather was a scholar of linguistics. He studied at Hanover College, Harvard University, and the University of Munich. He held faculty posts at Northwestern University (1903–1909) and the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (1909–1945).

William Austin Montriou was an Indology scholar and jurist. He served as Professor of Law and Jurisprudence at Presidency University (~1855–1869) and practiced as an Advocate at the Calcutta High Court (~1862).

William Blackstone was an academic scholar who completed his education at Charterhouse School (~1735–1738) and Pembroke College, Oxford (~1738–1745). He subsequently held a post at the University of Oxford (~1758–1766).

William Brian Rasmussen is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He completed an M.A. at the University of Texas at Austin in 1995 and was Matilal Lecturer in Indian Philosophy at King's College London (attested 2007–2008).

William Bright was a linguist and Indologist who studied at UC Berkeley under Murray Barnson Emeneau. He held posts at Deccan College, the U.S. Department of State, UC Berkeley, UCLA (1959–1988), and the University of Colorado Boulder (~1988–2006).

William C. Kirby is a scholar of sinology and history. He studied at Dartmouth and Harvard under Philip A. Kuhn. He held posts at Washington University in St. Louis (~1980–1992) and Harvard University, where he became Dean in 1992.

William Carey was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Golok Nath Sharma and Ramram Basu. He served as Professor of Sanscrit at Fort William College (1801–1830) and was Principal of Serampore College (1818–1832).
